Present law provides that when the state, a county or a municipality, or any or all of them, has recovered from the sale or rental of any property purchased by them, or any one, or any combination of them, moneys sufficient to pay the taxes for which the property was sold, it is the duty of the officers of such entity to report the recovery to the assessors of the county and municipality for assessment. Present law authorizes the county, and the municipality, or any or all of the officers who have an interest in the property, to convey the property to any other governmental entity meeting the conditions specified below. In order to receive property, a governmental entity must certify to such officers that the property is to be used for purposes that would make the property subject to condemnation by the governmental entity under its powers of eminent domain. The proper officers of the municipality or county may convey property permitted to be used for residential purposes to a private nonprofit entity that meets all the following conditions: (1) The entity is certified as a tax exempt entity under the Internal Revenue Code; (2) The entity is chartered to construct or to restore residential dwellings for the purpose of creating affordable housing for the disadvantaged and needy, and the property conveyed to the entity is used for that purpose; and (3) The property, once constructed or restored, is conveyed for use as an owner-occupied residence. In Shelby County present law authorizes the proper officers of the municipality or county to convey property purchased at a tax sale to the agency or commission of such municipality or county for redevelopment of properties certified under existing law, for those uses authorized by existing law, as amended by the Community Redevelopment Act of 1998. Additionally, in Shelby County, the governing body of the municipality or county may convey property to a nonprofit community development corporation for where use by the nonprofit community development corporation is deemed by the governing body of the municipality or county to inure to the benefit of the area the recipient nonprofit community development corporation is chartered or authorized to serve. In Shelby County, the proper officers of the municipality or county may convey properties with road frontage no greater than 24 feet acquired in tax sales to adjoining property owners. Present law authorizes the proper officers of the municipality or county to convey real property suitable for community gardening to a private nonprofit entity that meets all the following conditions: (1) The entity is certified as a tax exempt entity under the Internal Revenue Code; (2) The entity is qualified to operate and maintain a community garden; and (3) Any interest in or use of real property conveyed must revert to the municipality or county if the entity ceases to operate and maintain a community garden on the property. This bill deletes the above provisions regarding exemption from taxation on September 1, 2024.SATISFACTION OF DELINQUENCY AND REMOVAL FROM TAX ROLLS Whenever any property is sold at a tax sale and is purchased by the state, by a county, by a municipality, or by a county and municipality, this bill requires the officers of the state, or the county, or the municipality, or of county and municipality, purchasing the property, to notify the county trustee and the collector of any municipal taxes that are a lien upon the property, when actual possession has been taken of such lands, and the county trustee and the collector of municipal taxes are then authorized and directed to note the payment of the taxes, for which the sale was held upon the tax rolls. If actual possession is not taken by such entity, then the lands must not be removed from the tax rolls, nor must the lands be removed from the tax rolls, if the owner or former tenant is permitted to remain in possession of the property without the payment of rent to the state, county or municipality or county and municipality. This bill deletes these provisions on September 1, 2024.SALE OF LAND – COUNTY AS PURCHASER Present law provides that it is the duty of the county mayor of each county to take charge of all the lands bought in by the county at such delinquent tax sales. During the period when redemption of such tract of land can be made, the land must be (i) held and put only to a use that will not result in a waste of the land or (ii) sold to a third party, subject to the right of redemption. This bill adds to the present law by requiring the county mayor to cause a certified copy of all orders confirming the sale of a parcel to the county pursuant to existing law to be recorded in the office of the register of deeds of the county. This bill revises the present law by no longer requiring the land to be (i) held and put only to a use that will not result in a waste of the land or (ii) sold to a third party during the period when redemption of such tract of land can be made. Present law provides that after the period of redemption has elapsed, it is the duty of the county mayor to arrange for the disposition of every tract of such land as expeditiously and advantageously as possible unless parcels acquired by the county are identified by the county mayor, or the mayor's design as being in an area or zoning classification that would make the accumulation of larger areas advantageous to the parcels' reuse and redevelopment. The mayor may hold those properties until a sufficient number of parcels or area has been acquired to improve the parcels' marketability and redevelopment profile. In no event must this accumulation result in property being held without being marketed for more than five years. This bill deletes these provisions. Present law requires a committee of four members to be elected by the county legislative body, from the county legislative body, who, together with the county mayor, must place a fair price on each tract of land. Such committee may authorize the sale of any tract of land upon such terms as will secure the highest and best sale price, but the credit extended must not exceed three years and a lien must be retained to secure purchase price. This bill deletes these provisions. This bill, instead, authorizes the county legislative body may adopt regulations concerning sales of parcels purchased by the county at a delinquent tax sale. The regulations must be designed to promote a fair, effective, competitive, and transparent method of disposing of the parcels so as to attain the highest bid for each parcel. Present law prohibits a tract of land from being sold for an amount less than the total amount of the taxes, penalty, cost and interest, unless the legislative body, upon application, determines that it is impossible to sell the tract of land for this amount, and grants permission to offer the land for sale at some amount to be fixed by such legislative body. Interest must be calculated on the full amount of the taxes, penalty, cost and interest from the time of the acquisition of the land by the county until the sale thereof. This bill deletes these provisions and instead, requires each parcel to be offered for sale with no minimum bid or approval by the county legislative body required, unless otherwise required by the regulations adopted by the county legislative body. This bill authorizes the county mayor to solicit offers for one or more individual parcels or for all parcels on a list prepared pursuant to existing law. Any solicitation of offers must contain a statement as to how and where offers may be filed, and must be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county. The county is immune from liability for all dues, fees, and assessments secured by a lien upon the parcel purchased by the county at a delinquent tax sale if (i) offers are solicited for the parcel, (ii) s minimum amount is not established for a sale of the parcel; and (iii) an offer is not received within 30 days of the publication of the solicitation in a newspaper of general circulation in the county. Present law provides that whenever the sale of a tract of land is arranged by the county mayor, the deed must not be executed and the sale must not become final until 10 days after the publication in a newspaper published in the county of a notice of the proposed sale. If anyone, during such 10 days, increases the offer made for the land by 10 percent or more, the party making the first offer must be notified and a day fixed when both parties must appear and make offers. The tract of land must be sold to the party making the highest and best offer. This bill adds to the present law by clarifying that the county mayor must give notice to those persons filing offers to appear at a certain time, date, and location and must post the notice at a place available to the general public. At such time, date, and location, the county mayor or the county mayor's designee must conduct an auction of the parcel with the starting bid being the highest written offer received prior to the auction. All persons are eligible to offer bids at the auction. . If no raise offer is timely filed, the original bidder is the successful bidder. This bill authorizes the county mayor to approve the sale by internet sale of parcels purchased by the county at a delinquent tax sale. This bills requirements after a written offer is made may be waived by the county mayor as to parcels offered for sale by internet sale. The highest bidder at such internet auction is the successful bidder. This bill requires the proceeds derived from retentions or conveyances of parcels purchased by the county at a delinquent tax sale to be applied in the following order: (1) First, proceeds must be applied to reimburse the taxing entity for amounts paid by the taxing entity for the purchase of the parcel in the tax proceeding or which remain owing by the taxing entity; (2) Any proceeds remaining after the application of proceeds provided by (1) must be applied first to unpaid attorney fees allowed in the tax proceeding, then to other unpaid court costs, and then divided on a pro rata basis based upon the taxes levied against the parcel by the county and any other taxing entity which has filed a proceeding; (3) Any proceeds remaining after the application of proceeds provided by (1) and (2) must be applied to pay other taxes and accrued interest, penalties, and court costs, owed to the county and any other taxing entity on a pro rata basis, based upon the amounts of taxes owing each; and (4) Any proceeds remaining after the application of proceeds provided by (1)-(3) inure to the benefit of the county. This bill requires the parcel to be released from all taxes, penalties, interest, and court costs owing all tax entities, up to the date of the conveyance subject only to any current year taxes that may not have been paid pursuant to this bill. Any conveyance or retention of a parcel that occurs before the expiration of the redemption period remains subject to the right of redemption. A conveyance or retention of a parcel does not affect the redemption period applicable to the parcel. This bill provides that the county mayor is not required to seek approval of the county legislative body to supervise the sale and conveyance of each parcel unless (i) otherwise required by the regulations adopted by the county legislative body, or (ii) the county legislative body has determined to retain or convey the parcel pursuant to this bill. Present law authorizes the county to, upon a majority vote of its legislative body determining it in the best interests of the county to use the property for a public purpose, decide to retain ownership and possession of such property. This bill adds to the present law by requiring a document evidencing the determination of the county legislative body to retain ownership of a parcel to be recorded in the office of the register of deeds. The county may retain ownership of the parcel, or it may, subject to such terms as may be agreed upon, transfer ownership of the parcel to the following: (1) A governmental entity; or (2) A nonprofit entity; provided, that the parcel is transferred in accordance with this bill. To be eligible to receive a parcel pursuant to (2) above, this bill requires a nonprofit entity to comply with the following requirements: (1) The entity must be exempt from federal income taxation under the Internal Revenue Code; (2) The entity must agree that the conveyed parcel must be used by the entity for at least a reasonable period for the purposes for which the entity was chartered; and (3) The entity is chartered to: (i) construct or to restore residential dwellings for the purpose of creating affordable and habitable housing for the disadvantaged and needy citizens of the community; (ii) construct or to restore historical properties or buildings in the community; (iii) operate or maintain a community garden in the community; or (iv) construct, operate, or maintain a park, memorial, or gathering place in the community, available for use by the general public. Present law requires conveyances of the land to be made without warranties of any sort, and deeds must be executed by the county mayor or other chief fiscal officer of the county. The deed must be prepared by the back-tax attorney as a part of the duties for which the attorney is compensated, and no additional compensation is allowed. This bill revises the present law and, instead, requires deeds to be executed by the county mayor only. This bill adds to the present law by providing that he execution of a deed constitutes a certification by the county that all procedures and rules of the county have been complied with and that all interest of the county in the parcel is being conveyed. The certification must not be overturned absent clear and convincing evidence of a substantial and material violation of a statutorily mandated requirement. If the county mayor determines that there may be a defect in the title to the parcel, then present law authorizes the county mayor to move the court in which the parcel was sold in the tax proceeding to take action to cure the defect. This bill adds to the present law by requiring a diligent effort to give notice of any such motion to be made as to all interested persons as of the date of the filing of the motion. This bill provides that if a municipality does not authorize the county to convey its interest in tax parcels, or if a municipality files a complaint to collect delinquent property taxes owing the municipality separate from the complaint filed by the county to collect delinquent property taxes owing the county, then the municipality's governing body and chief executive officer must dispose of the parcels purchased by the municipality at a delinquent tax sale. In such event, the municipality's legislative body has the powers and duties of the county legislative body as set out in this bill and existing law; its chief executive officer has the powers and duties of the county mayor as set out in this bill and existing law; and the municipality stands in the place and stead of the county. Present law authorizes the county mayor to make an evaluation of the parcel conveyed to a county pursuant to a tax lien sale of property to determine whether the value of the parcel or amount of money the county is likely to receive if the county sold the parcel exceeds the financial obligations or environmental risks associated with the parcel. If the county mayor determines that such financial obligations or environmental risks exceed the value of the parcel, the county legislative body may adopt a resolution, by a 2/3 vote, concurring in the county mayor's determination and directing the county mayor to request relief from the court in which the parcel was sold. If the court finds that the motion should be granted, then the court may rescind its prior order. In the event the prior order is rescinded, title to the parcel must be deemed to have remained in that state which existed as of the date of entry of the prior order confirming the sale. The court has broad discretion to ensure that this does not result for any period of time in the creation of a parcel for which no person or entity has responsibility. The court may then appoint a special master and direct the special master to conduct a second sale of the parcel upon such terms and conditions as may be ordered by the court. This bill adds to the present law by requiring such relief to be sought by motion pursuant to the Tennessee Rules of Civil Procedure filed within 120 days after the entry of the order confirming the sale. This bill also clarifies that these provisions apply to the risks of an individual parcel only and does not apply to the aggregated risks of all or multiple parcels bid in to the county. Present law authorizes, in the event no person presents a bid at the second sale of the parcel, the court to thereafter approve a negotiated sale of the parcel upon such terms and conditions as may be ordered by the court or such other relief as the court may order. This is applicable to the financial obligations or environmental risks of an individual parcel only and must not be applicable to the aggregated financial obligations or environmental risks of all or multiple parcels bid in to the county. This bill adds to the present law by also authorizing the court to approve a negotiated sale of the parcel upon such terms and conditions as may be ordered by the court or such other relief as the court may order as an alternative to ordering a second sale. This bill also authorizes the court to allow an additional fee to the delinquent tax attorney for services rendered in regard to a negotiated sale of a parcel as provided in the law regarding property taxes.LISTING OF PARCELS Present law requires the county mayor to cause to be prepared and maintained a listing of all parcels owned by the county acquired pursuant to a tax lien sale of property. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill adds to the present law by requiring the assessor of property to assist the county mayor. Present law also requires the chief executive officer of a municipality to cause to be prepared and maintained a listing of all parcels owned by the municipality acquired pursuant to a tax lien sale of property. However, that the listing may omit any property that is required to be listed by a county by the county mayor. The listings must be prepared no later than July 1, 2018. The listings must be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county or posted on the local government website with a notice of the posting published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill changes the present law by, instead, requiring, the listings to be prepared annually by July 1. Present law authorizes each list or notice published to contain a solicitation for offers to purchase the parcels listed and a statement as to how and where such offers may be filed. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill changes the present law by requiring, instead of authorizing, each list or notice published to contain a solicitation for offers to purchase the parcels listed and a statement as to how and where such offers may be filed.SALE OF LAND GENERALLY Present law requires the court to order a sale of the land for cash, certified funds, cashier's check, money order, or automated clearing house transfer, as applicable. All sales are subject to the equity of redemption. Such sale may be conducted electronically in lieu of public outcry. At all sales, the clerk of the court, acting for a tax entity or entities prosecuting the suit, must bid the debt ascertained to be due for taxes, interest, penalties, and the costs and fees incident to the collection thereof, where no other bidder offers the same or larger bid. However, when the legislative body of a tax entity determines that the environmental risks or financial liabilities associated with the property are such that it is not in the best interests of the tax entity for a minimum bid to be offered at the tax sale, the clerk must not offer a bid on the property at the tax sale. Present law requires, for every county except Pickett County, Trousdale County, Clay County, Jackson County, Macon County, Smith County, Scott County, Wilson County, and Sumner County, up to 10 percent of the sale proceeds to be applied first to payment of any unpaid balance of compensation due the prosecuting attorney. Second, the proceeds of the sale must be applied to the costs of the suits. Third, the remainder must be applied to the state first, county second, and municipality third, the amount due each to be ascertained by a decree of the court. This bill deletes these provisions. Present law also requires, for every county except Pickett County, Trousdale County, Clay County, Jackson County, Macon County, Smith County, Scott County, Wilson County, and Sumner County, the proceeds from such sale to be applied first to the payment of the 10 percent penalty allowed as compensation for prosecuting the suits, second to the costs, and third the remainder to be applied to the state first, county second, and the municipality third, the amount due each to be ascertained by a decree of the court. This bill deletes this provision. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill requires the tax sale proceeds to be distributed according to the following priorities: (1) Amounts owing the delinquent tax attorneys prosecuting the cause; then (2) The costs of the proceeding exceeding the attorneys' fees; then (3) Amounts owing the taxing entities which are parties in the cause; then (4) Amounts owing to tax entities filing a claim for current and other delinquent taxes and interest due them as stated in claims filed in response to notices sent them pursuant to existing law and for which no action has been filed pursuant to the law regarding property taxes, divided prorated upon the amount of the base taxes due each; then (5) Any other property taxes and expenses owing any taxing entity secured by a tax lien on the parcel; then (6) Any remaining proceeds must be distributed in accordance with the law regarding a motion setting for claim to excess sale proceeds. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill provides that if there are not sufficient funds to pay all of the amounts stated in (1)-(3) above, then the tax liens of the taxing entities securing such amounts must lapse upon expiration of the redemption period, it being the intent of the general assembly that a parcel sold at a tax sale be conveyed free of any remaining tax liens other than taxes levied for the current year. However, a taxing entity retains any personal right of action it may have against prior owners of the parcel. If the tax sale is subsequently invalidated or declared void, then the lapsed tax liens must be reinstated retroactively. Starting on September 1, 2024, if a taxing entity purchases a parcel pursuant to this bill, this bill requires the taxing entity to pay to the clerk all amounts owing as court costs, including the amount owing the attorney prosecuting the case, within 60 days after the order confirming the sale becomes final. The taxing entity may by motion request the court for an extension of time in which to pay such amount. The court may grant such extension for such period as the court determines proper not to exceed three years and may award interest to accrue during such extension at a rate determined by the court. In making such determinations, the court must consider the financial condition of the taxing entity. If the taxing entity determines to retain the parcel, it must within 60 days of making such determination, pay to the clerk all remaining amounts owing on the parcel. If the parcel is subsequently transferred pursuant to the law regarding the sale of land where a county is the purchaser for an amount greater than the court cost paid pursuant to bill, such excess must be distributed pursuant to this bill to the extent funds are available. Any remaining amounts owing on the parcel must be dismissed by the court and the liens securing the same must terminate. Starting on September 1, 2024, this bill authorizes the court to order the sale of all or a portion of the taxable personal property constituting a parcel secured by a tax lien. Such sale must be made according to such procedures as may be established by the court. Upon a tax proceeding being filed to enforce a tax lien against real or personal property, any requirement mandating the confidentiality of records pertaining to the parcel terminates.TAXES ON WHICH LIEN BASED This bill provides that each person owning an interest in a corporate entity or similar organization and that is, or is stated in the records of the office of secretary of state to be, an inactive, dissolved, revoked, or otherwise terminated entity, is jointly and severally liable with the entity, each other, and such other persons as may be liable, for all unpaid property taxes levied against parcels assessed to the entity, and such interest, attorney fees, and other court costs as may accrue on the same.INDEMNITY BOND OF PLAINTIFF Present law prohibits a sheriff or other officer from being required to levy an execution on any property the title of which is disputed, or to sell the same after levy, unless the plaintiff will first give bond and security to such officer, to indemnify the sheriff or other officer against all damages and costs in consequence of the levy or sale. This bill adds that the bond or security is not required if the execution is issued in a proceeding to collect delinquent property taxes.ADVANCE FEES ON PROCESS FROM OTHER COUNTIES Present law prohibits a sheriff or constable from being compelled to execute any subpoena or original summons in civil cases coming from any county other than the one in which such sheriff or constable is an officer, unless the fees allowed such sheriff or constable by law for the service of such process, if demanded, are paid in advance. This bill provides that this provision does not apply to summons, executions, or other orders of a court rendered in a proceeding to collect delinquent property taxes.SEARCH DURING EXECUTION This bill requires, in all proceedings for the collection of delinquent property taxes, an officer serving an execution issued in such proceeding to conduct a search of the person of the defendant and such items and areas under the control of the defendant and to seize such cash, property, and other assets belonging to the defendant, as is necessary to satisfy the execution and such additional fees as may be incurred by the officer. If the defendant objects to the search, then the defendant must reduce the defendant's objections to writing and give them to the officer. Then the defendant must be escorted by the officer to appear before a judicial commissioner or other official authorized to issue warrants, to state the defendant's grounds for the objection. The commissioner must determine the validity of such grounds and either grant or refuse to allow the search. The commissioner must retain the written objections of the defendant and the commissioner's written decision and deliver both to the clerk of the court from which the execution issued. This bill provides that the exemptions set out in the law regarding execution for criminal cases, and homestead exemptions and such other laws that provide that exemptions do not apply to sales of property of the defendant in regard to sales for taxes include executions issued in proceedings for the collection of delinquent property taxes.DILIGENT EFFORT TO GIVE ACTUAL NOTICE As used in the present law regarding property taxes, "diligent effort to give actual notice of the proceedings" means a reasonable effort to give notice that is reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances and conditions, to apprise interested persons of the pendency of the proceedings in time to afford them an opportunity to prevent the loss of their interest in the parcel. Such effort must be such as one desirous of actually informing the persons might reasonably adopt to accomplish it. Such effort does not, however, require that an interested person receive actual notice. Nor does it require the plaintiff to search records or sources of information in addition to that information available in the specific offices listed in existing law. This bill adds to the definition of "diligent effort to give actual notice of the proceedings" by clarifying that the effort does not require the tax entity or delinquent tax attorney to obtain discovery.NATURE OF PROCEEDINGS This bill provides the following: (1) The law regarding adjustments and refunds for collection and enforcement relevant to taxes and licenses does not apply to property taxes; (2) The law regarding judicial or trusts sales does not apply to property tax proceedings, tax liens, or the enforcement of such tax liens; (3) An interested person must not file as a defense, a counterclaim, a cross claim or for another purpose, a defense or cause of action not directly related to the tax proceeding, or a claim of a set off; and (4) The failure of a defendant or interested person in a tax proceeding to have exhausted all administrative remedies bars the defendant from contesting an issue in the tax proceeding that could have been decided in such manner.COLLECTION BY GARNISHMENT Present law authorizes the county trustee to proceed against a taxpayer who is delinquent in the payment of tangible personal property taxes by retaining an agent to collect such delinquent tangible personal property taxes, plus interest authorized by law, reasonable costs, and legal fees, provided that the collection activities are in compliance with present law. If a collection agent is retained, then the county trustee must utilize the bidding procedures applicable to the county to select and retain the agent and must notify the county legislative body of such action. The agent's collection fee must not exceed 30 percent of tangible personal property taxes due, and the fee must be added to the total amount of delinquent tangible personal property taxes owed, plus interest authorized by law, reasonable costs, and legal fees. Present law prohibits a contract or other arrangement entered into to retain a collection agent from providing that the compensation paid to the agent is conditioned on increasing tangible personal property tax collections in the county involved. A contract found to contain such language is void and unenforceable. An agent must not communicate with the delinquent taxpayer or proceed upon the delinquent taxpayer's property unless authorization to take such action is provided in the contract. The agent must not institute or undertake a collection or related activity in violation of the Tennessee Collection Service Act. An agent retained must be licensed and in good standing with the Tennessee collection service board. Present law requires all foreclosures, seizures, litigation, or other judicial or non-judicial proceedings to enforce a tax lien or any similar rights to collect delinquent tangible personal property taxes, plus interest authorized by law, reasonable costs, and legal fees, to be in the name of the taxing jurisdiction as the plaintiff or claimant. An agent who also performs audit procedures must not be retained to collect delinquent tangible personal property taxes. This bill clarifies that the above provisions and the contract authorized in the above provisions does not repeal or modify a provision of the law regarding property taxes.PROCEDURE FOR REDEMPTION OF PROPERTY Present law requires, in any motion to enforce a right of redemption brought by a transferee against a tax sale purchaser or other interested party, the tax sale purchaser or other interested party in whom the right of redemption originally vested to be served with a copy of the motion to redeem. This bill replaces this provision and, instead, requires in any motion to enforce a right of redemption brought by a transferee against a tax sale purchaser or other interested party, the movant to serve a copy of the motion to redeem upon the tax sale purchaser, each grantee of the tax sale purchaser's interest in the parcel, and all other interested persons as of the date the motion to redeem is filed, in the manner set forth in the Tennessee Rules of Civil Procedure for pleadings not asserting new or additional claims for relief. Present law requires, upon the filing of the motion to redeem and the payment of the required amount, the clerk to within 10 days send a notice of the filing of the redemption motion to the purchaser and all persons entitled to redeem the parcel. The notice of redemption must state the amount paid at the time of the filing of the motion and refer the persons to the existing law. This bill changes the present law by requiring the clerk to within 10 days send a notice of the filing of the redemption motion to each grantee of the tax sale purchaser's interest who has filed notice of the purchase and a mailing address with the clerk, instead of to all person entitled to redeem the parcel. This bill also requires the notice to be forwarded to the last known address of the addressee. Present law authorizes the purchaser to within 30 days after the mailing of the notice of redemption, file a response seeking additional funds to be paid by the proposed redeemer to compensate the purchaser for amounts expended by the purchaser for the purposes set out in existing law. The response must specifically set out the basis for each category of additional funds claimed. The response may also allege that the motion to redeem was not properly or timely filed. If no response is timely filed, the court must determine whether the redemption has been properly made, and if so, must cause an order to be entered requiring the proposed redeemer to pay additional interest at the rate set forth in existing law, accruing from the date the motion to redeem was filed until the date of such payment. This bill changes the present law by requiring, instead, if no response is timely filed, the court to determine whether the redemption has been properly made, and if so, must cause an order to be entered declaring the parcel redeemed. Present law provides that additional sums to be paid by the proposed redeemer at the demand of the purchaser include additional interest at the rate set out in existing law, accruing from the date the motion to redeem was filed until the date the purchaser's response was filed. If the court determines that the purchaser has not delayed consideration of the motion to redeem and that any response filed by the purchaser for additional funds was based on a reasonable expectation that the expenditures of the purchaser were reimbursable, then the court may require the proposed redeemer to also pay additional interest at the same rate, accruing from the date the purchaser's response was filed until the date of such payment. This bill adds to the present law by providing that if the court determines that disposition of a redemption motion has been unreasonably delayed, the court may decline or limit an award of additional interest under this present law.NOTICE OF TAXPAYER SUIT Present law provides that the return of the receipt signed by the defendant, spouse, or other person deemed appropriate to receive summons or notice as provided for in the Rules of Civil Procedure, or its return marked "refused", "unclaimed", or other similar notation, as evidenced by appropriate notation of such fact by the postal authorities, and filed as a part of the record by the clerk is evidence of actual notice and must be grounds for a default judgment. Process and notices delivered by registered or certified mail or by an alternative delivery service, with a return receipt, to an interested party's registered agent at the agent's address or to the address of the interested party, each as shown on the corporate records of a state secretary of state or other officer responsible for maintaining such records, must be sufficient to bind the interested party as to notices and service of process. This bill adds to the present law by providing that as used in the above provisions, "appropriate notation of such fact by postal authorities" includes tracking records located on the website of the delivery service. If a copy of the tracking records is filed with the clerk confirming the delivery, then the filing of the return receipt is not required. ON APRIL 22, 2024, THE HOUSE ADOPTED AMENDMENTS #1 AND #2 AND PASSED HOUSE BILL 2624, AS AMENDED. AMENDMENT #1 makes the following changes: (1) Revises the provision in the bill that deletes the present law (i) authorizing the corporation to provide written notice to the clerk and master in advance of a delinquent property tax sale auction held that it wishes to enter the minimum bid for cash for any parcel advertised for sale in such auction, and such minimum bid preempts all other bids for the parcel, and the local land bank must be the prevailing bidder; and (ii) providing that if there are no other bidders on a parcel, then such minimum bid must be accepted for no cash, and the local land bank must be the prevailing bidder and take title to the parcel in the same manner as a municipality bidding the minimum by revising that present law instead of deleting it. This amendment revises (ii) and, instead, provides that if a party other than the local land bank submits a bid for an amount greater than the minimum bid submitted by the local land bank pursuant to (i), the high bidder is the prevailing bidder, and the local land bank may, within two business days from the close of the tax sale auction, submit and deposit with the clerk of the court a revised bid for the parcel in an amount equal to, or greater than, the bid amount submitted by the high bidder. If the local land bank submits an equal or higher bid for the parcel within two business days of the close of the tax sale auction, then the local land bank is the prevailing bidder. However, this does not alter or modify the redemptive rights of any party. This amendment also provides that (i) and (ii) above only applies in Shelby County; (2) Deletes the provision in the bill that deletes the present law providing that commencing upon the date of transfer of any real property from a land bank to a taxable person or entity, if approved by local government, then the land bank is entitled to receive payments from the local government equal to 50 percent of real property taxes collected by the local government for a period of five years; (3) Deletes the provision in the bill providing that the county is immune from liability for all dues, fees, and assessments secured by a lien upon the parcel purchased by the county at a delinquent tax sale if (i) offers are solicited for the parcel; (ii) a minimum amount is not established for a sale of the parcel; and (iii) an offer is not received within 30 days of the publication of the solicitation in a newspaper of general circulation in the county; (4) Revises the provision in the bill providing that as an alternative to ordering a second sale or if a person does not present a bid at the second sale of the parcel, the court may thereafter approve a negotiated sale of the parcel upon such terms and conditions as may be ordered by the court or such other relief as the court may order, including, but not limited to, the conveyance to a nongovernmental entity claiming contractual rights to dues or assessments by no longer authorizing such other relief as the court may order, including, but not limited to, the conveyance to a nongovernmental entity claiming contractual rights to dues or assessments; (5) Deletes the provision in the bill clarifying that the Neighborhood Preservation Act does not apply to (i) liens securing the payment of property taxes, interest thereon, and court costs in proceedings to enforce the lien; (ii) tax sales conducted pursuant to the law regarding property taxes; (iii) parcels sold or ordered by a court to be sold at tax sales; or (iv) a requirement or provision in the law relevant to taxes and licenses; (6) Deletes the provision in the bill providing that a receiver's lien created under the "Neighborhood Preservation Act" is secondary to a first lien securing property taxes; (7) Deletes the provision in the bill that revises the present law providing that the filing of a petition for a judgment in rem acts as a bar of any transfer of title of the subject parcel or of any interests pertaining to such subject parcel, including transfers by tax sale or other foreclosure, transfers or creation of lien interests in the subject parcel, or otherwise, from the date of the filing until the petition is dismissed or until specific orders of the court authorizing a transfer of title, if the petition has attached a certificate of public nuisance by removing a tax sale from the list of transfers of titles; (8) Deletes the provision in the bill providing that the receiver's lien is a first lien on the subject parcel, which is superior to all prior and subsequent liens or other encumbrances associated with the subject parcel with the exception of liens securing the payment of property taxes as set out in the law regarding property taxes; (9) Deletes the provision in the bill that deletes the present law providing that the county trustee is allowed a credit pursuant to existing law for any local taxes and assessments that are not collected as a result of the failure of the receiver's lien sale to receive a cash payment for the minimum bid; and (10) Deletes the provision in the bill providing that the sale procedures set out in the "Neighborhood Preservation Act" do not apply to tax sales conducted pursuant to the law regarding property taxes. AMENDMENT #2 revises the effective date provision such that, for the following provisions, the effective date is September 1, 2024: (1) If the receiver's lien is not satisfied by the owner, requires the court to direct the receiver to offer the subject parcel for sale in accordance with the following: sale procedures set out in the Neighborhood Preservation Act do not apply to tax sales conducted pursuant to state property tax law; (2) Establishes that the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program does not apply to (i) liens securing the payment of property taxes, interest thereon, and court costs in proceedings to enforce the lien; (ii) tax sales conducted pursuant to state property tax law; (iii) parcels sold or ordered by a court to be sold at tax sales; or (iv) a requirement or provision set out in state law relative to taxes and licenses; (3) Establishes that a corporation created pursuant to the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program to operate a land bank has the power, as limited by the legislative body of the crating local government(s), to bid at a tax sale conducted pursuant to state property tax law, subject to the same procedures and requirements applicable to other bidders. In addition, the corporation may negotiate and complete purchases and leases of parcels purchased at tax sales by counties and cities, subject to the same procedures and requirements applicable to other governmental entities; (4) Removes the following present law provisions: (A) The corporation may provide written notice to the clerk and master in advance of any delinquent property tax sale auction that it wishes to enter the minimum bid for cash for any parcel advertised for sale in such auction, and such minimum bid must preempt all other bids for said parcel, and the local land bank shall be the prevailing bidder; (B) If there are no other bidders on a parcel under (A), such minimum bid must be accepted for no cash, and the local land bank must be the prevailing bidder and take title to said parcel in the same manner as a municipality bidding the minimum bid; and (C) Commencing upon the date of transfer of any real property from a land bank to a taxable person or entity, if approved by local government, the land bank must be entitled to receive payments from the local government equal to 50 percent of real property taxes collected by the local government for a period of five years; and (5) Establishes that the corporation has the power to pay any unpaid taxes due and owing by the owner of record of the real property, or make any government mandated improvements to the property.

title: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 7, relative to accreditation.
abstract: Education, Higher - As enacted, makes changes relative to a governing board of a public institution of higher education determining the institutional accrediting agencies or associations eligible to serve as an accreditor; prohibits an accrediting agency or association from compelling a public institution of higher education to violate any state law. - Amends TCA Title 49, Chapter 7.
summary: This bill requires the Tennessee higher education commission ("commission") and each governing board of a public institution of higher education in this state to regularly update their rules regarding accreditation to conform with changes made by, and to take advantage of new flexibilities and data sources made available by, the U.S. department of education or by an enactment of the congress of the United States. By December 31, 2024, this bill requires the following: (1) The commission to identify and determine the accrediting agencies or associations best suited to serve as an accreditor for public institutions of higher education in this state. Such accrediting agencies or associations must be recognized by the database created and maintained by the United States department of education; and (2) The commission and each governing board of a public institution of higher education in this state to amend their rules regarding accreditation to ensure that each institution may choose to pursue accreditation by any accreditor recognized by the U.S. department of education for the types of educational programs offered by the institution. This bill prohibits an accrediting agency or association from compelling a public institution of higher education in this state to violate any state law. Any adverse action taken against any such institution based, in whole or in part, on the institution's compliance with any state law constitutes a violation of this bill that may be enforced in accordance with this bill, but only to the extent that the state law is preempted by a federal law recognizing the necessity of the accreditation standard or requirement. This bill authorizes a public institution of higher education in this state that is negatively affected by retaliatory or adverse action taken against the institution by an accrediting agency or association to bring a civil action against the accrediting agency or association in a court of competent jurisdiction in this state, and to obtain liquidated damages in the amount of the federal financial aid received by the institution, in addition to the institution's court costs and reasonable attorney fees. This bill authorizes the commission to promulgate rules, as it deems necessary, to implement this bill. ON APRIL 1, 2024, THE SENATE ADOPTED AMENDMENT #1 AND PASSED SENATE BILL 2528. AMENDMENT #1 rewrites the bill to, instead, require each governing board of a public institution of higher education in this state to regularly update the institution's policies and practices regarding institutional accreditation to conform with changes made by the U.S. department of education or by the U.S. congress. By December 31, 2024, each governing board of a public institution of higher education in this state must identify and determine the institutional accrediting agencies or associations eligible to serve as an accreditor. Such institutional accrediting agencies or associations must be recognized by the database created and maintained by the U.S. department of education. By December 31, 2024, each governing board of a public institution of higher education in this state must update the institution's policies and practices regarding accreditation to ensure that the institution may freely choose to pursue accreditation by any accreditor recognized by the U.S. department of education for the kinds of programs offered by the institution. This amendment prohibits an accrediting agency or association from compelling a public institution of higher education in this state to violate any state law. Any adverse action taken against a public institution of higher education in this state based, in whole or in part, on the institution's compliance with any state law constitutes a violation of this amendment that may be enforced in accordance with this amendment, but only to the extent that the state law is not preempted by a federal law recognizing the necessity of the accreditation standard or requirement. A public institution of higher education in this state that is negatively affected by a violation of this amendment may bring a civil action against the accrediting agency or association in a court of competent jurisdiction in this state. If an accrediting agency or association violates this amendment, then the governing board of the public institution of higher education must notify the general assembly in writing within 30 calendar days of the violation. ON APRIL 16, 2024, THE HOUSE SUBSTITUTED SENATE BILL 2528 FOR HOUSE BILL 2625, ADOPTED AMENDMENT #2, AND PASSED SENATE BILL 2528, AS AMENDED. AMENDMENT #2 makes technical corrections.

title: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 29 and Title 48, relative to business entities.
abstract: Business Organizations - As introduced, requires incorporators of a corporation to provide at least five days' notice, rather than two days' notice, before holding an organizational meeting to elect directors or a board of directors to complete the organization of the corporation if initial directors are not named in the charter. - Amends TCA Title 29 and Title 48.

title: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 67, Chapter 4, Part 17, relative to taxation.
abstract: Taxes, Privilege - As introduced, repeals the professional privilege tax for tax years that begin on and after June 1, 2025. - Amends TCA Title 67, Chapter 4, Part 17.
